definitions.explanation: Plants that grow in the sea, used in Japanese cuisine and other applications.

examples.japanese: {海藻|かいそう}は{健康|けんこう}にいい。
examples.english: Seaweed is good for your health.

examples.japanese: {海藻|かいそう}サラダを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
この{地域|ちいき}では{海藻|かいそう}の{養殖|ようしょく}が{盛|さか}んだ。
examples.english: Seaweed farming is thriving in this region.

examples.japanese: {海藻|かいそう}にはミネラルや{食物繊維|しょくもつせんい}が{豊富|ほうふ}に{含|ふく}まれている。
examples.english: Seaweed is rich in minerals and dietary fiber.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{昔|むかし}から{海藻|かいそう}を{食|た}べる{文化|ぶんか}があり、{昆布|こんぶ}やわかめなど{種類|しゅるい}も{豊富|ほうふ}だ。
examples.english: Japan has a long tradition of eating seaweed, with a wide variety including kombu and wakame.

notes:
TYPES:
Common edible seaweeds in Japan:
・{昆布|こんぶ} (kombu/kelp) - used for dashi
・わかめ (wakame) - used in miso soup, salads
・{海苔|のり} (nori) - used for sushi, onigiri
・ひじき (hijiki) - dark seaweed, often simmered
・もずく (mozuku) - slimy seaweed, eaten with vinegar
・めかぶ (mekabu) - root of wakame

USAGE:
・{海藻|かいそう}サラダ (seaweed salad)
・{乾燥|かんそう}{海藻|かいそう} (dried seaweed)
・{海藻|かいそう}を{採|と}る (to harvest seaweed)

NUTRITION:
Seaweed is valued in Japan for its minerals (iodine, calcium), fiber, and umami. It's a staple of washoku ({和食|わしょく}).

NOTE:
Not to be confused with {海草|かいそう} (sea grass, a different type of marine plant).
